program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = inputs.gravity; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const t = time; const tossedVelocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const tossedAcceleration = -gravity; const tossedHeight = launchSpeed * t - (gravity * t * t) / 2; const isAtTop = t >= apexTime; const dropVelocity = isAtTop ? -gravity * (t - apexTime) : 0; const dropAcceleration = isAtTop ? -gravity : 0; const dropHeight = isAtTop ? apexHeight - (gravity * (t - apexTime) * (t - apexTime)) / 2 : apexHeight; let tossState = "At launch"; if (t > 0 && t < apexTime) tossState = "Rising"; else if (Math.abs(t - apexTime) < 0.05) tossState = "At the top"; else if (t > apexTime && tossedHeight > 0) tossState = "Falling"; else if (t >= apexTime && tossedHeight <= 0) tossState = "At launch height"; let dropState = "Held in place"; if (Math.abs(t - apexTime) < 0.05) dropState = "Just released"; else if (t > apexTime && dropHeight > 0) dropState = "Falling together"; else if (t >= apexTime && dropHeight <= 0) dropState = "At launch height"; const pxScale = 120; const baseY = 340; const tossX = 180; const dropX = 460; const ballY = (h) => baseY - h * pxScale; const objects = []; objects.push(...sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 50, w: 260, h: 350, title: "Toss", state: tossState, id: "lane.toss" })); objects.push(...sdk.panel({ x: 340, y: 50, w: 260, h: 350, title: "Drop", state: dropState, id: "lane.drop" })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.toss", { x: tossX, y: baseY, length: 2.2 * pxScale, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.2, ticks: [0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0], label: "Height", unit: "m" })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.drop", { x: dropX, y: baseY, length: 2.2 * pxScale, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.2, ticks: [0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0], label: "Height", unit: "m" })); const ty = ballY(Math.max(0, tossedHeight)); const dy = ballY(Math.max(0, dropHeight)); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.toss", tossX, ty, 26, { role: "output" })); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.drop", dropX, dy, 26, { role: "output" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.v.toss", { x: tossX - 25, y: ty }, { value: tossedVelocity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "v" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.a.toss", { x: tossX + 25, y: ty }, { value: tossedAcceleration, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "a" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.v.drop", { x: dropX - 25, y: dy }, { value: dropVelocity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "v" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.a.drop", { x: dropX + 25, y: dy }, { value: dropAcceleration, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "a" })); if (!isAtTop) { objects.push(sdk.gate("gate", dropX, ballY(apexHeight), { open: false, label: "Apex Gate" })); } else { objects.push(sdk.gate("gate", dropX, ballY(apexHeight), { open: true, label: "Apex Gate" })); } objects.push(...sdk.callout(tossX + 45, ty - 20, ["v: " + sdk.format(tossedVelocity) + " m/s", "a: " + sdk.format(tossedAcceleration) + " m/s^2"], { id: "callout.toss" })); objects.push(...sdk.callout(dropX + 45, dy - 20, ["v: " + sdk.format(dropVelocity) + " m/s", "a: " + sdk.format(dropAcceleration) + " m/s^2"], { id: "callout.drop" })); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects, readouts: [{ id: "tossedVelocity", value: tossedVelocity }, { id: "tossedAcceleration", value: tossedAcceleration }, { id: "dropVelocity", value: dropVelocity }, { id: "dropAcceleration", value: dropAcceleration }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed, gravity, apexTime, apexHeight, tossedVelocity, tossedAcceleration, tossedHeight, dropVelocity, dropAcceleration, dropHeight } }; }

manifest.title: Zero velocity isn’t zero acceleration.
manifest.summary: At the top, velocity is zero for an instant, but gravity keeps changing it. A release gate drops a second ball then, letting both fall together.
manifest.description: Two side-by-side vertical lanes show a tossed ball and a dropped ball. Arrows display their velocities and accelerations, and callouts show exact numerical values as time progresses.
assumptions: No air resistance, the same gravity for both balls, up is positive.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed or gravity, then press Play. Use the scrubber or At top button to examine the instant velocity hits zero.
